sugestoes.texto: When credential sync is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `Response` (the raw `fetch` result), but several callers consume the return value as the parsed token object. `googlecalendar` reads `res?.data` (undefined on a Response, so `token.access_token` throws), `hubspot` reads `.expiresIn` (undefined → `NaN` expiry), and `zoho-bigin`/`zohocrm` read `.data.error` (TypeError on undefined). Each caller must branch on the response type, or the helper must normalize the synced response to the same shape the refresh function returns before returning.

`refreshOAuthTokens(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId)` expects a user id as its third argument, but `credentialId` (the credential's own id) is passed here. In sync mode this sends `calcomUserId: <credentialId>` to the sync endpoint, so the wrong user's credential is looked up/refreshed. Pass the credential's user id instead.

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the whole `SafeParseResult` (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed credential, but this result object is written directly into `prisma.credential.key`. The stored key becomes `{ success, data }` instead of the credential fields, corrupting the credential for later reads. Persist `key.data` (the parsed object) instead.

When the response has no `refresh_token`, the helper injects the literal string `"refresh_token"` into the parsed data. For providers whose schemas require `refresh_token: z.string()` (zoom, webex, office365), this passes validation and the bogus token is persisted, so the next real refresh call sends an invalid refresh token and fails. Preserve the existing refresh token from the caller instead of substituting a placeholder.

`refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `Response` in sync mode, but this code immediately accesses `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` and `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.access_token`, which are `undefined` on a Response and throw a TypeError. The sync-path return must be handled (e.g. `await response.json()`) before reading `.data`.

The webhook secret is compared with `!==`, a non-constant-time comparison, on a value that gates writing arbitrary third-party credentials for any user id supplied in the body. An attacker able to observe response timing can progressively recover the shared secret. Use a constant-time comparison (e.g. `crypto.timingSafeEqual`) on equal-length buffers.

When credential sync is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `Response` object from `fetch`, but in the default branch it returns `refreshFunction()`'s parsed value; callers such as zohocrm (`zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`) and zoho-bigin (`tokenInfo.data.error`) treat the result as the parsed token body. The two branches return incompatible shapes, so the sync path dereferences `.data` on a `Response` and token refresh silently fails. Normalize the return value (e.g. `await response.json()`) so both branches yield the token object callers expect.

The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is the calcom user id, but `credentialId` (the credential's primary key) is passed here. When sync mode is active the endpoint receives a credential id as `calcomUserId`, so it refreshes/fetches credentials for the wrong user (or none). Pass the owning user id (`credential.userId`) instead.

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the whole `SafeParseResult` (`{ success, data }`), but this code stores that wrapper directly as the credential key. The credential `key` column now holds `{ success, data }` instead of the parsed token, corrupting the persisted Google credentials. Use the unwrapped value (e.g. `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data`) for the `key` field.

When the response omits `refresh_token`, the helper injects the literal string `"refresh_token"` into the parsed data. Callers persist this data back to the credential (e.g. googlecalendar `data: { key }`), so a missing refresh token silently overwrites the stored token with the placeholder string and breaks future refreshes. Preserve the existing refresh token or reject the response instead of substituting a constant.

`refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `Response` in sync mode, but this code immediately reads `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` and later `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.access_token`. A `Response` has no `.data`, so the property is `undefined` and the branch always falls into the error path, leaving the token unrefreshed. Await `response.json()` before accessing the body fields.

The webhook secret is compared with `!==`, a non-constant-time comparison, on a value that gates writing arbitrary users' third-party credentials. An attacker can recover the secret byte-by-byte via timing differences and then inject credentials for any user. Compare using a constant-time function such as `crypto.timingSafeEqual`.

issues.descricao: The new app-credential webhook checks its shared secret with a plain !== string comparison instead of a constant-time comparison, leaking timing information about the secret.

comentarios.texto: Direct !== comparison of webhook secret leaks via timing attack. Use constant-time comparison (e.g., crypto.timingSafeEqual on hashed/buffered values with length check) instead of `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.

The webhook authenticates a secret using direct string inequality, which is not constant-time and can leak information about the secret through comparison timing. Compare fixed-length representations using a constant-time primitive (such as crypto.timingSafeEqual), handling absent or malformed headers safely, instead of comparing the secret strings directly.

The webhook secret is compared with the `!==` operator, which short-circuits on the first differing byte and leaks the secret via response timing (timing attack). An attacker can iteratively recover CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET and then forge requests that create/update arbitrary user credential keys (decrypted with the AES key) via this endpoint. Use a constant-time comparison, e.g. crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers, guarding for length mismatch first.

issues.descricao: The webhook parses the body with zod .parse and decrypts/JSON-parses the keys without error handling, so invalid payloads produce 500 errors instead of 400 responses.
issues.textoGolden: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: zod parse, symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse throw unhandled (no try/catch) with no method guard. WHY: Invalid body/keys or GET request crashes handler with 500 and leaks stack, instead of 400/405. HOW: Wrap parse/decrypt in try/catch returning 400 and restrict to POST.

schema .parse plus symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse throw unhandled (ZodError, decrypt error, SyntaxError) on invalid body or tampered keys, crashing webhook with 500. Use safeParse and try/catch with 400 responses.

issues.descricao: The webhook's non-atomic findFirst-then-create lets concurrent deliveries for the same user and app insert duplicate credential rows.

comentarios.texto: The webhook performs a non-atomic findFirst followed by create when no credential exists. Concurrent deliveries for the same user and app can both observe no row and insert duplicates because Credential has no unique userId/appId constraint; subsequent findFirst updates only one duplicate, leaving competing credentials stale. Serialize the lookup/create operation for each user/app pair or introduce an appropriate uniqueness constraint and atomic upsert.

issues.descricao: parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when the refresh response omits a refresh token, so the stored credential gets an invalid refresh token and later refreshes fail.
issues.textoGolden: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

comentarios.texto: The parser fabricates the literal refresh token "refresh_token" whenever a successful response omits refresh_token, including when synchronization is disabled. Office365's response schema explicitly permits that omission, and its caller merges parsed data over existing credentials, replacing the valid saved refresh token with this invalid value and breaking the next refresh. Leave the property absent so the existing token survives the merge.

When a refresh response omits refresh_token, this helper manufactures the hardcoded credential "refresh_token". Callers such as Office365 merge this into stored credentials, overwriting the valid existing refresh token and causing subsequent provider refreshes to use a predictable invalid token. Leave the field absent and preserve the existing credential when omission is allowed by the provider, or reject the response when a refresh token is required; do not substitute a literal authentication token.

WHAT: Missing refresh_token is replaced with literal string "refresh_token". WHY: Stores bogus refresh token in DB, breaking all future refreshes and masking provider errors. HOW: Preserve existing credential refresh_token or throw instead of injecting placeholder.

issues.descricao: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys from z.string().toString(), which produce a literal key rather than a wildcard, so the sync-mode schema does not validate or keep expiry and other token fields as intended.
issues.textoGolden: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

comentarios.texto: `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to a fixed string key such as "ZodString", so minimumTokenResponseSchema requires a literal numeric property with that name. Every synced token response fails validation and throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Use `z.object({access_token: z.string()}).passthrough()` instead.

The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]", not a wildcard. The schema therefore requires a numeric property named "[object Object]", so safeParse always fails in credential-sync mode and the function throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Use `.passthrough()` on an object with access_token and optional numeric expiry fields instead.

The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` evaluate to a literal string like "ZodString" and not to a wildcard. The schema therefore requires a numeric property with that nonsense name and never matches real token responses. In sync mode every refresh throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Use `.passthrough()` and a real expiry check instead.

issues.descricao: In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but callers expect their provider-specific shapes (res.data, axios .data, HubspotToken), so token refresh breaks for Google, Zoho and HubSpot when credential sharing is on.
issues.textoGolden: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

comentarios.texto:
WHAT: In the credential-sharing branch `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch` `Response` object instead of a parsed token payload, yet several callers treat the result as an already-parsed token object.
WHY: Callers such as hubspot (`hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn`), zoho-bigin (`tokenInfo.data.error`), zohocrm (`zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`) and googlecalendar (`res?.data`) read `.data`/token fields off the return value; a `Response` has neither, so the sync path yields `undefined`/`NaN` or throws a TypeError — the feature's primary code path is broken for those apps.
HOW: Parse the response (e.g. `const data = await response.json(); return data;`) before returning, or make every caller await the appropriate response handler.

In sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response (no `.data`), but the google caller reads `res?.data` and then `token.access_token`, throwing a TypeError swallowed by the catch, so the token is never refreshed.

`res?.data` assumes the value returned by refreshOAuthTokens has a `.data` field (true for the `fetchTokens.res` branch), but when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED the helper returns a raw `fetch()` Response, which has no `.data`. Then `token.access_token` throws. Either parse the shared-mode Response here or have refreshOAuthTokens return a normalized `{ data }` shape.

issues.descricao: Google Calendar persists the safeParse result object instead of its data as the credential key, corrupting the stored credential so later reads fail.
issues.textoGolden: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

comentarios.texto: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a SafeParse result {success,data}, not the parsed key. Storing it directly as `key` writes the wrapper to the credential. Unwrap like other callers: check .success and use .data.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns SafeParse result {success,data}, but call site stores that wrapper as credential `key` (previously googleCredentialSchema.parse() returned the plain object). Store `key.data` / handle wrapper, otherwise persisted credential becomes {success,data} shape and subsequent credential reads fail.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns SafeParse wrapper {success,data} but code stores the whole wrapper as credential.key. Office365calendar in same PR unwraps via .data. Persisted credential will be {success,data} instead of tokens, so next load fails validation. Unwrap to .data after success check.

issues.descricao: After switching to parseRefreshTokenResponse, the tokenResponse.success check in Office365 refreshAccessToken is dead code and the previous error logging was dropped.

comentarios.texto: parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws when parsing fails, so the `tokenResponse.success` check on the next line is dead code and the previous error logging was removed. A failed refresh now throws out of refreshAccessToken instead of keeping the old credentials. Catch the error or restore the previous handling.

issues.descricao: Salesforce getClient now refreshes the OAuth token and writes the credential on every service construction, adding a network round trip and DB write even when the access token is valid.

comentarios.texto: getClient now unconditionally exchanges the Salesforce refresh token on every service construction, even when the saved access token is valid. Each constructor invocation adds a blocking OAuth network round trip and credential database write before any Salesforce operation, replacing jsforce's existing on-demand refresh behavior. Keep refresh on demand or guard the exchange with a token-expiration check.

issues.descricao: The new Salesforce token refresh uses prisma without importing it, so the code fails type checking and throws a ReferenceError at runtime.

comentarios.texto: The new credential update references prisma without importing or declaring it; searching this file finds only the new usage. This fails TypeScript checking and raises ReferenceError after a successful token exchange at runtime. Import prisma from @calcom/prisma before using it.

issues.descricao: Zoho Bigin passes the credential id instead of the user id to refreshOAuthTokens, so the sync endpoint receives the wrong calcomUserId.
issues.textoGolden: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

comentarios.texto:
WHAT: The 3rd argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is `credentialId` (= `credential.id`, line 53), but the function's parameter is `userId` (`refreshOAuthTokens(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId)`).
WHY: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED, the sync endpoint is sent `calcomUserId: <credential id>` instead of the user id, so Bigin credentials are synced against the wrong/non-existent user (all other apps correctly pass `credential.userId`).
HOW: Pass `credential.userId` instead of `credentialId` as the third argument.

refreshOAuthTokens' third parameter is the Cal.com userId (used as `calcomUserId` in the sync request and to decide whether sharing runs), but this call passes `credentialId`. Every other caller passes `credential.userId`, so the credential-sync endpoint receives a credential row id as the user id and shared credentials are fetched/updated for the wrong identity. Pass `credential.userId` here.

refreshOAuthTokens' third parameter is `userId` (declared in refreshOAuthTokens.ts line 3 and used as `calcomUserId: userId.toString()`), but this call passes `credentialId` (the Credential row id, line 53) instead of the user id. When credential sharing is enabled the customer's sync endpoint receives a credential id labelled as calcomUserId and cannot resolve the correct Cal.com user. Pass `credential.userId` (the BiginToken/credential payload carries it) or plumb the user id through refreshAccessToken.

issues.descricao: Salesforce checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok when refreshing the token, which can misclassify successful responses, and then ignores the refreshed token.
issues.textoGolden: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Checks response.statusText !== "OK" instead of response.ok and builds jsforce.Connection from stale credentialKey.access_token/instance_url ignoring accessTokenParsed.data. WHY: Refresh never takes effect (old token reused) and valid refreshes can throw on runtimes where statusText is empty. HOW: Check !response.ok and use parsed access_token/instance_url for connection and DB update.

issues.descricao: After refreshing the Salesforce token, jsforce.Connection is created with the stale access_token and instance_url instead of the newly refreshed values.
issues.textoGolden: The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

comentarios.texto:
WHAT: The new block fetches and persists a fresh access token (`accessTokenParsed.data`) but then creates the `jsforce.Connection` with the stale `credentialKey.access_token` (line 106) instead of the just-refreshed token.
WHY: The refreshed token is written to the DB but never used for the connection; if the old token was expired, jsforce must refresh again (extra round trip) or fail, and the DB/connection state diverge.
HOW: Pass the new access token (`accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`) to the `jsforce.Connection`.

issues.descricao: The app-credential webhook looks up appStoreMetadata by app.slug, but the map is keyed by dirName, so apps whose slug differs from their directory (e.g. google-calendar) always get a 404 and their credentials cannot be synced.

sugestoes.texto: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` combines `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`, but `isTeamAdmin` (packages/lib/server/queries/teams/index.ts:264) already returns true for role ADMIN or OWNER. The `&&` therefore only holds for team OWNERs, so a team ADMIN who is not the organizer or an attendee is rejected with FORBIDDEN by the check at line 54 — the exact opposite of the variable's intent. Use `||` so either an admin or an owner passes.

`sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is passed the raw input `guests`, but the database was updated only with `uniqueGuests` (already-present attendees and BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS removed at lines 74-78). In `sendAddGuestsEmails` (packages/emails/email-manager.ts:541), `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` selects the full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` for entries considered newly added, so an existing attendee or blacklisted address still present in `guests` is wrongly treated as a new guest and receives the wrong email. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead of `guests`.

`this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` dereferences the first attendee without a guard, so building the nodemailer payload throws a TypeError when `attendees` is empty. The parent `OrganizerScheduledEmail.getNodeMailerPayload` (organizer-scheduled-email.ts:50) uses `this.calEvent.title` and never indexes attendees; use an optional access (e.g. `this.calEvent.attendees[0]?.name`) or the same title-based approach.

`isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`, but `isTeamAdmin` already matches memberships with role ADMIN or OWNER (packages/lib/server/queries/teams/index.ts:264-284), so requiring both makes the flag true only for actual OWNERs and denies plain team ADMINs; `isTeamAdmin` also returns a membership object while `isTeamOwner` returns a boolean, so the `&&` yields a mixed-type value. Use `||` (or a single admin-or-owner helper) so admins and owners both pass the permission check.

`sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is passed the raw input `guests`, but the booking was updated only with `uniqueGuests` (deduped and blacklist-filtered at lines 74-106). In sendAddGuestsEmails the routing `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` (packages/emails/email-manager.ts:541) then compares against emails that were never persisted, so blacklisted/duplicate addresses in the raw input are treated as valid new guests. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead so the email logic matches the persisted attendees.

issues.descricao: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so only team owners pass; team admins who are not organizer or attendee are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN.
issues.textoGolden: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with && instead of ||. WHY: isTeamAdmin returns truthy for role ADMIN or OWNER while isTeamOwner returns true only for OWNER, so the && expression is only true for OWNERs; team ADMINs are treated as unauthorized and get FORBIDDEN when adding guests, contradicting the variable's intent. HOW: use `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) || (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0))`.

The flag is named `isTeamAdminOrOwner` but is computed with `&&` (both admin AND owner). A team admin who is not the owner, or the owner who is not flagged admin, will fail this check, so the guard at line 54 wrongly throws FORBIDDEN for legitimate admins/owners. Use `||` between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner.

The variable `isTeamAdminOrOwner` names an OR condition, but the code combines `isTeamAdmin(...)` and `isTeamOwner(...)` with `&&`, so it is true only when the user is both admin AND owner. Either the name is wrong or the operator is; as written the permission check at line 54 denies a plain team admin, contradicting what the identifier promises. Use `||` to match the name (or rename if AND is intended).

issues.descricao: The guest blacklist is lowercased but incoming guest emails are compared without normalization, so a blacklisted address submitted with different casing bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and is added and emailed.
issues.textoGolden: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The blacklist is compared case-sensitively against guest input while blacklistedGuestEmails are lowercased. WHY: blacklistedGuestEmails entries are lowercased but the filter compares `guest` verbatim (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`); an authenticated user can add a blacklisted address simply by changing its case (e.g. `Foo@bar.com` vs `foo@bar.com`), bypassing the configured BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restriction. HOW: normalize the guest before comparison, e.g. `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest.toLowerCase())`.

Case-sensitivity bypass of the guest blacklist. `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased on the list side (line 71) but the input side is compared raw: `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` (line 77). A guest email submitted with any different casing (e.g. `Foo@Bar.com` when the blacklist holds `foo@bar.com`) passes the filter and is persisted, defeating BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS. Normalize the input before comparison, e.g. filter on `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest.toLowerCase())` (and likewise lowercase `guest` for the attendee dedup check).

WHAT: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries are lowercased but the incoming guest string is compared without lowercasing/normalizing. WHY: an attacker bypasses the blocklist with case variation (e.g. Spam@Example.com) and gets added/emailed.

issues.descricao: The server never deduplicates the guests array, so a request with the same email twice inserts duplicate attendee rows for the booking.
issues.textoGolden: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: uniqueGuests filter only dedupes against existing booking.attendees with case-sensitive === and never dedupes duplicates within the input guests array itself (server schema has no uniqueness refine unlike the client). WHY: a request with the same new email twice creates duplicate attendee rows via createMany.

uniqueGuests filters only against existing attendees/blacklist but never dedupes guests[] itself and schema has no uniqueness check. A request like guests=[a@x.com,a@x.com] passes the filter twice and createMany inserts duplicate attendee rows or throws an unhandled DB unique-constraint exception. Dedupe/normalize input (and reject intra-request duplicates) before createMany.

uniqueGuests filters against existing attendees but does not deduplicate addresses within the incoming guests array. A direct mutation with the same new address twice inserts two Attendee records and sends duplicate invitations because the server schema permits duplicates and the Attendee model has no unique booking/email constraint. Deduplicate normalized input before filtering and inserting.

issues.descricao: Check-then-insert without a transaction or unique constraint lets two concurrent addGuests calls for the same email both pass the existing-attendee check and create duplicate attendees.

comentarios.texto: Race condition: findFirst check for existing attendees then booking.update+createMany is not atomic. Two concurrent addGuests calls with the same new email both see it as absent and both insert, creating duplicates. Guard with a unique constraint and handle conflict or run in a transaction/serializable check.

Check-then-insert race: the handler reads `booking.attendees` at the start, filters against it, then inserts in a separate `prisma.booking.update ... createMany` with no transaction or unique guard. Two concurrent addGuests calls for the same guest both see it as absent and both insert, producing duplicate attendees. Wrap the read+filter+insert in a transaction (or rely on a unique constraint on (bookingId, email) and handle the conflict) so concurrent requests cannot both succeed.

issues.descricao: Attendee authorization and existing-attendee dedup compare emails case-sensitively, so an attendee with differently-cased stored email is FORBIDDEN and a case-variant of an existing attendee is added again.

comentarios.texto: Inconsistent email normalization for identity checks. Both the authorization check `attendee.email === user.email` (line 52) and the existing-attendee dedup `guest === attendee.email` (line 76) use strict case-sensitive equality, while emails are treated as case-insensitive everywhere else in this handler (the blacklist block directly below lowercases). Consequence: a legitimate attendee whose stored casing differs from their session email is wrongly FORBIDDEN, and a guest differing from an existing attendee only by case is duplicated rather than filtered. Compare on a normalized form (both sides `.toLowerCase()`), consistent with the blacklist normalization.

issues.descricao: The handler passes the unfiltered guests list to sendAddGuestsEmails, which uses it to pick who gets AttendeeScheduledEmail, so existing attendees included in the request receive a new-booking confirmation instead of the add-guests email.
issues.textoGolden: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) passes the raw input guests instead of the filtered uniqueGuests. WHY: already-existing attendees included in the request are misclassified as newGuests in email-manager and receive AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail (wrong notification).

Dead-transform / wrong input: `uniqueGuests` is computed (dedup vs existing attendees + blacklist) and written to DB, but `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the original `guests`. Existing attendees re-submitted are then `includes()`-matched as new and get AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. Pass `uniqueGuests`.

Pass `uniqueGuests` (the filtered set written to DB) to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of raw `guests`; the email layer assumes newGuests exactly equals newly created attendees for its Scheduled vs AddGuests branch.

issues.descricao: EventManager is created with the requesting user's credentials, so when a non-organizer adds guests the organizer's calendar event is not updated (or the wrong account is used) for references without a credentialId.

comentarios.texto: EventManager is initialized with the requesting user's credentials rather than the booking organizer's credentials. When an attendee or team owner adds guests to a booking whose calendar reference lacks credentialId, updateAllCalendarEvents selects credentials by type from the caller's calendars, so the organizer's event is not updated or the update targets the wrong account. Load credentials for booking.userId and initialize the manager with the booking owner.

issues.descricao: Claims a failing calendar update at addGuests.handler.ts:165 aborts the mutation after guests are persisted; the calendar update path already swallows provider errors.

comentarios.texto: The attendees are written to the database at line 92, but `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` at line 165 runs outside the try/catch. If it throws, the mutation returns an error even though the guests are already persisted, so the DB and the calendar are out of sync. No emails are sent, and a retry then fails with 'emails_must_be_unique_valid'. Catch and handle the calendar update failure after the DB write.

The attendees are already committed to the DB when `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` is awaited without a try/catch. If the calendar sync throws, the mutation returns an error and skips the emails, although the guests were added. The caller sees a failure for a partly applied change and may retry. Handle calendar sync failure as best-effort, as the email send is, or run it before the DB write.

issues.descricao: Claims any attendee can add guests and trigger invites; this is the deliberate permission model of the new feature.

comentarios.texto: Any attendee, matched only by email, is allowed to add arbitrary guests to a booking, and the handler then sends emails and calendar invites on the organizer's behalf. Any attendee can use this to send invites to arbitrary addresses. Restrict the action to the organizer and team admins, or verify that the attendee's email is confirmed.

issues.descricao: The guests array has no server-side size limit, so any authorized caller, including an attendee, can add thousands of guests and trigger an unbounded batch of inserts and emails.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: guests is an unbounded z.array(z.string().email()) with no max length. WHY: any authorized caller (including a mere attendee) can submit thousands of emails causing unbounded createMany inserts plus unbounded Promise.all email fanout in sendAddGuestsEmails.

The mutation accepts an unbounded guest array that is persisted and immediately expanded into concurrent emails to every attendee. For non-seated bookings each email's ICS serializes the full attendee list, so adding N guests creates O(N) concurrent sends and O(N²) aggregate attachment work; repeated additions also resend to all existing attendees. Enforce a server-side guest-count and total-attendee limit before insertion and bound notification concurrency.

issues.descricao: The Remove email tooltip in MultiEmail is a hard-coded English string instead of a translation key.

comentarios.texto: Tooltip content="Remove email" is hard-coded English user-facing text bypassing i18n while surrounding strings in the same file/PR use t(). Wrap it in t() e.g. content={t("remove_email")} and add the key to locales.

`Tooltip content="Remove email"` is a hard-coded English user-facing string, while the surrounding code in this same component routes user text through `t()` (e.g. `t("add_another")` on line 69). This string bypasses the translation mechanism and will never be localised; it should use a translation key.

The new removal tooltip hard-codes `Remove email`, so users in non-English locales see English text even though the neighbouring controls use `t(...)` and this component already obtains `t` from useLocale. Route this tooltip through a translation key (and supply its English translation) rather than using the literal.

issues.descricao: The onError fallback to unable_to_add_guests is unreachable because the template-string message is always truthy.

comentarios.texto: Unreachable fallback: `message` is a template string `${code}: ${...}` which is always truthy, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` never takes the fallback. Build message conditionally or test the underlying parts for emptiness.

In `onError`, `message` is always a non-empty template string (`"${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}"`), so the fallback `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` is unreachable and the newly added `unable_to_add_guests` translation is never shown. The user is instead shown a raw error code prefix like `BAD_REQUEST: ...` rather than the translated message; the fallback and code prefix handling should be corrected so the intended translated text reaches the user.

The error message is built as a template string, so it is always truthy. The `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback is therefore dead code, and the user can see "undefined: ..." or an untranslated raw message. Use `err.message ? t(err.message) : t("unable_to_add_guests")`.

issues.descricao: After a validation failure followed by a successful add, isInvalidEmail stays true, so the stale emails_must_be_unique_valid error shows the next time the dialog is opened.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: addGuestsMutation onSuccess resets multiEmailValue and closes the dialog but never resets isInvalidEmail. WHY: after one failed validation the red emails_must_be_unique_valid error persists on the next open/successful add.

issues.descricao: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings, so hosts and attendees receive add-guests emails even when standard emails are disabled.
issues.textoGolden: The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

issues.descricao: The add-guests handler omits booking.iCalUID from the CalendarEvent, so the add-guests emails' .ics attachments use booking.uid as UID and recipients' calendars treat them as a new event rather than an update of the original booking invite.
The addGuests FORBIDDEN error uses the translation key you_do_not_have_permission, which is missing from the locale files, so the dialog shows the raw key to users.
The comment in MultiEmailLazy.tsx ("These are like 40kb") is copied from the phone input lazy loader and does not apply to MultiEmail, which only uses existing UI components.
addGuests does not check the booking status, so guests can be added to cancelled or rejected bookings, which updates calendars and emails invitations for events that no longer exist.
Guest email uniqueness is checked case-sensitively, so case variants of the same address are accepted as distinct guests (and slip past the lowercased blacklist).
Adding guests ignores `seatsPerTimeSlot`, so a seated event can exceed its configured capacity; reject when attendees plus new guests exceed the seat limit.

sugestoes.texto: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` calls `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym`, but `SiteSetting.default_locale` can return nil (the getter in lib/site_setting_extension.rb:420-428 returns `c[name]`, a Hash lookup that yields nil when the setting is not yet loaded, and the `shadowed_by_global` path at line 106 can also set it to nil) — precisely the not-fully-loaded state the PR description says this change exists to handle. `nil.to_sym` raises NoMethodError, and since `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` runs from `set_locale`, a `before_filter` on every request, this crashes the request instead of falling back. Guard the value, e.g. use `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym if SiteSetting.default_locale` or default to `:en` before calling `to_sym`.

With fallbacks enabled by this PR, the result of `translate` now depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale` (it is part of the fallback chain built in `FallbackLocaleList#[]`), but the cache key at line 72 is `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"` and omits the site default locale, and `@cache` is never cleared when the setting changes. Changing the site default locale therefore keeps serving translations resolved under the old fallback order until a full `reload!`, producing stale/wrong-language output. Include the effective fallback order (e.g. `SiteSetting.default_locale`) in the cache key or invalidate the cache on locale-setting changes.

Fallback lookup now resolves through `SiteSetting.default_locale` and `:en`, but those fallback locales are only eagerly loaded by `ApplicationController#set_locale` (the only caller of `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!`), while `I18n.translate` lazily loads only `config.locale`. Any translation performed outside a controller request — background jobs setting `I18n.locale = SiteSetting.default_locale` (app/jobs/base.rb:151) and `I18n.with_locale(user.effective_locale)` (app/services/post_alerter.rb:138, lib/post_destroyer.rb:102) — will fall back to a locale that was never loaded and return missing translations instead of the intended English/site text. Load the fallback list inside the translate path itself (e.g. ensure each locale in `I18n.fallbacks[config.locale]` is loaded before `translate_no_cache`) so fallbacks work regardless of request context.

With fallbacks enabled by this PR, the result of `translate` now depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale` (it is part of the fallback chain built in `FallbackLocaleList#[]`), but the cache key at line 72 is `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"` and omits the site default locale, and `@cache` is never cleared when the setting changes. Changing the site default locale therefore keeps serving translations resolved under the old fallback order until a full `reload!`, producing stale/wrong-language output. Include the effective fallback order (e.g. `SiteSetting.default_locale`) in the cache key or invalidate the cache on locale-setting changes.

issues.descricao: Fallback locale catalogs are only loaded in the controller's set_locale filter, while translate loads just the current locale, so translations outside requests (jobs, mailers) cannot fall back to the site default or English.

comentarios.texto: Fallback catalogs are ensured loaded only in the controller filter, leaving non-controller translation paths without the catalogs required by the newly enabled fallback backend. Jobs::Base sets I18n.locale directly and PostAlerter uses I18n.with_locale, while the accelerator loads only the current locale and backend fallback lookups bypass that loader; missing keys therefore still produce missing translations or skip the configured site fallback until another request happens to load those catalogs. Ensure the full fallback chain is loaded at the translation boundary, rather than relying solely on the controller filter.

The new fallbacks contract requires the fallback locales (site default and :en, from FallbackLocaleList#[]) to be loaded before Backend::Simple#translate is asked for them — Backend::Simple only returns already-loaded translations. This PR added I18n.ensure_loaded!/I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! but wired it only into ApplicationController#set_locale, and the loader that actually gates every translation, I18n.translate (line 68), still loads only `config.locale`. As a result, any I18n.t performed outside the request cycle (console, background jobs, mailers) or before set_locale runs will not load the fallback locales and will silently return 'translation missing' instead of the fallback the new I18n.fallbacks advertises. Fix: have translate ensure the fallback chain is loaded (e.g. call I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! / load the fallback locales here), not rely on the controller hook.

translate loads only config.locale, but the new fallback chain (default_locale, :en) is loaded only by the controller's I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!. Outside controllers (jobs, mailers, rake), a key missing in the current locale falls back to a locale that is not loaded, so it returns 'translation missing', and the LRU cache then stores that result. Fix: in translate, call I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! (or load each locale in fallbacks[config.locale]) before the lookup.

issues.descricao: The translation cache key does not include the site or its default locale, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so multisite processes or a changed default locale serve stale fallback translations.

comentarios.texto: The new fallback order depends on SiteSetting.default_locale, but the accelerator's translation cache does not include that setting or the current site in its key. In a multisite process, two sites with the same user locale and different default locales reuse the first site's cached fallback translation; changing the default locale also leaves cached fallback results stale. Include the effective fallback chain or site/default-locale context in the translation cache key.

sugestoes.texto: `getClientsWithPermission` collects `resource.getName()` for every resource of type `Clients`, which includes the all-clients type resource whose name is the literal `"Clients"` (created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` with name = type), in addition to the per-client resources named after the client id. The only caller, `AvailableRoleMappingResource.getRoleIdsWithPermissions`, feeds these strings to `realm.getClientById(cid)`, so the literal `"Clients"` yields a null `ClientModel` and an NPE; the previous implementation in `ClientPermissions` stripped a name prefix before returning ids, and this override dropped that normalization. Filter out the type resource (e.g. skip when `AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE.equals(resource.getName())` or resolve the name to a real client id) before adding it to the granted set.

The listener now runs under `Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` and calls `clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false)` / `roles().setPermissionsEnabled(...)` / `groups().setPermissionsEnabled(...)`, but when the V2 provider is selected `management(...)` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2` whose `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled` (ClientPermissionsV2.java:193) unconditionally throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. Deleting a client (or removing a role/group) with the fine-grained-authz flag enabled therefore fails with an unhandled exception in the event listener; guard the call for the V2 provider or make the V2 implementation a no-op instead of throwing.

getClientsWithPermission adds resource.getName() for every resource of type 'Clients', which includes the all-clients resource whose name is the literal type 'Clients' (AdminPermissionsSchema creates it with name=type at lines 247-252). The caller AvailableRoleMappingResource.getRoleIdsWithPermissions (line 230) does realm.getClientById(cid).getRolesStream() with no null check, so the 'Clients' entry yields getClientById('Clients') == null and throws an NPE when a permission grants a scope to all clients. Skip resources whose name equals AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE (or guard the null client in the caller).

The ClientRemovedEvent branch calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), but under the V2 feature management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whose clients() is ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException (ClientPermissionsV2.java:193-195). Deleting a client while ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled therefore fails in the removal listener. Guard the V2 case (skip the call when V2 is active) or implement a no-op setPermissionsEnabled in ClientPermissionsV2.

issues.descricao: Claims the removal-cleanup listener is guarded by the V1 fine-grained flag, so client/role/group permissions are orphaned when V1 is disabled or only V2 is enabled.
issues.textoGolden: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

comentarios.texto: The cleanup is now entirely wrapped in Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), so when the feature is disabled the pre-existing removal cleanup (roles/clients/groups .setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)) no longer runs. Realms using the non-V2 permission model will keep orphaned authorization resources/permissions after a client, role or group is removed. The gate should preserve the old behavior when the feature is off (run for V1), or the V1 cleanup must be performed elsewhere.

issues.descricao: getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.
issues.textoGolden: In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

issues.descricao: Claims getResourceTypeResource can return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, causing a NullPointerException in findByResource.
issues.textoGolden: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.

issues.descricao: ClientPermissionsV2 has an unused private getEvaluationContext method.
issues.textoGolden: Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

comentarios.texto: Dead computation: `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` is private and has no caller anywhere in the class. Its only possible consumer in the V1 class, `canExchangeTo`, was overridden to throw UnsupportedOperationException (line 148-150). The EvaluationContext and its overridden getBaseAttributes are built and then never used — remove the method (or wire it into canExchangeTo if token-exchange is meant to be supported).

issues.descricao: The Javadoc of the void requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() methods says they return true instead of documenting that they throw ForbiddenException.

comentarios.texto: The Javadoc for `void requireView()` says "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}", but requireView() is void and throws ForbiddenException rather than returning a value. It is a copy-paste of the canView() doc and should read "Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canView()} returns {@code false}", matching the sibling require* methods (requireListClientScopes, requireConfigure, etc.).

The Javadoc for `void requireViewClientScopes()` says "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}", but the method is void and throws ForbiddenException. The doc describes a boolean return the method never produces; it should state that it throws ForbiddenException if canViewClientScopes() returns false, consistent with the other require* methods.

Declaration does not match the method it documents: the javadoc for `requireView()` ('Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}.') and for `requireViewClientScopes()` ('Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}.') describes a boolean-returning accessor, but both methods are declared `void` and are the require* counterparts that throw ForbiddenException (as documented for requireManage/requireConfigure above). The text was copy-pasted from the corresponding can* methods; it should state that the method throws when canView()/canViewClientScopes() is false.

issues.descricao: ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.

comentarios.texto: canView() does not recognize an all-clients MANAGE permission even though canView(client) grants viewing through canConfigure(client) and canManage(client). For an administrator with global MANAGE but no VIEW, ClientsResource.getClients selects an unpaginated realm-wide client stream and evaluates authorization for clients before applying pagination, instead of fetching the requested database page. Include the global MANAGE permission in the global viewing capability while preserving client-specific denial semantics.

issues.descricao: canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

comentarios.texto: The global VIEW check returns true before evaluating client-specific VIEW permissions, bypassing a negative permission on an individual client. An administrator granted VIEW on all clients can therefore read a client explicitly excluded by a client-specific denial; ClientsResource.getClients also bypasses per-client checks when this evaluator's parameterless canView() returns true. Evaluate the specific client resource before falling back to the all-clients permission, and ensure listing does not use a global grant to skip specific denials.

Do not short-circuit resource-specific view evaluation on the global fine-grained VIEW grant. With an all-clients VIEW permission allowing an administrator and a client-specific VIEW permission denying that administrator, canView() returns true here and the specific client permission is never evaluated. This differs from the specific-over-global override behavior exercised for users in this PR and exposes the denied client's representation. Keep the administrative-role bypass separate from fine-grained grants and evaluate the client's resource before falling back to the all-clients resource; also ensure the global view result used by client listing cannot bypass those overrides.

issues.descricao: The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

comentarios.texto: The expected ForbiddenException can come from getDefaultClientScopes(), before removeDefaultClientScope() is invoked. With no permission granted, the initial read is forbidden, so this test still passes if removal's manage-permission check is removed entirely; the later granted removal also succeeds in that broken implementation. Obtain the scope ID using the privileged realm client outside this try block, then invoke only removeDefaultClientScope() through the restricted client and assert that it is forbidden.

issues.descricao: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.

sugestoes.texto: `resetState` clears `password`, `errorMessage`, and `step` but leaves `backupCodes`, `backupCodesUrl`, `dataUri`, and `secret` populated, and it never calls `URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl)`. Closing the modal after enabling 2FA therefore leaves the plaintext backup codes and the blob URL resident in component state for the lifetime of the page, and each subsequent setup leaks another object URL. Clear these fields and revoke the URL in `resetState`.

The signature change to `disable(password: string, code: string, backupCode: string)` makes `backupCode` a required parameter, but the sibling caller `apps/web/components/security/DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:38` still calls `TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable(password, totpCode)` with two arguments, which is a TypeScript arity error. Give `backupCode` a default (`backupCode?: string` or `backupCode = ""`) or update the other caller.

`resetState` resets only `password`, `errorMessage`, and `step`, leaving `backupCodes`, `backupCodesUrl`, `dataUri`, and `secret` from the previous setup in state. Reopening the modal after a completed setup shows the stale QR/secret/backup codes and a stale object URL instead of starting fresh. Clear the remaining state (and revoke `backupCodesUrl`) inside `resetState`.

issues.descricao: The credentials authorize() skips the password check when any totpCode is present, and the new backup-code branch never validates that totpCode, so a backup code plus a dummy totpCode logs in without the account password.

comentarios.texto: The new backup-code branch authenticates without guaranteeing the password check ran: password verification at line 121 is gated on `!credentials.totpCode`, and the branch at line 131 triggers on any truthy `credentials.backupCode` regardless of that gate. A POST to the credentials callback supplying a valid backup code together with any non-empty totpCode therefore takes the backup branch (skipping TOTP validation) while line 121 skips password verification — granting a session using only a second-factor backup code, with no account password. Require the password check before the backup branch, or include backupCode in the guard at line 121 (e.g. `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode && !credentials.backupCode)`).

The backup-code branch accepts a valid backup code even when an arbitrary nonempty totpCode has skipped password verification. The preceding guards at lines 113–125 trust the presence of totpCode, but this new branch does not validate it, allowing a holder of a backup code to log in to a password account without knowing its password by submitting both fields. Require password verification for backup-code authentication rather than allowing an unverified totpCode to bypass it.

WHAT: The new backup-code login branch authenticates without verifying the password when credentials also contain any totpCode value (password check at line 121 is skipped when totpCode is truthy, and the backup branch never checks it). WHY: An attacker holding only a backup code can add a dummy totpCode to the credentials callback and log in without the password, reducing two factors to one. HOW: Verify the password whenever backupCode is used (or decouple the password check from totpCode presence).

issues.descricao: After enabling 2FA, onEnable is only called from the backup-codes Close button; dismissing the dialog by Escape/overlay never notifies the parent, so the settings page keeps showing 2FA disabled.

comentarios.texto: On a successful enable (response.status === 200) the modal no longer calls onEnable(); it only advances to SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes, and onEnable() is now invoked solely from the 'close' button (line 269). If the user dismisses the Dialog via ESC or an overlay click, DialogContent's onOpenChange fires (wired to a plain setEnableModalOpen toggle at apps/web/pages/settings/security/two-factor-auth.tsx:64 and the conditional render at apps/web/components/security/TwoFactorAuthSection.tsx:36), so onEnable never runs. The parent callbacks (setEnableModalOpen(false) + utils.viewer.me.invalidate() / setEnabled(true)) are skipped, leaving the 2FA Switch unchecked and the UI showing 2FA as disabled even though the server has enabled it. Call onEnable() from the dismiss path (onOpenChange) or when transitioning into DisplayBackupCodes, not only from the Close button.

Successful enablement no longer invokes onEnable until the backup-code screen's explicit Close button is clicked. Dismissing that screen through the dialog's onOpenChange instead only closes it in the parent and does not invalidate viewer.me, leaving the settings switch showing disabled even though the server has enabled 2FA. Ensure dismissal after successful enablement also invokes the completion callback and resets the setup state.

After a successful enable, `onEnable()` is no longer called and is only called from the backup-codes Close button. If the user dismisses the dialog by Escape or overlay click (`onOpenChange`) while the codes are displayed, the parent is never notified that 2FA is enabled. The modal also keeps its step state and the plaintext backup codes. Call `onEnable` when 2FA is enabled, or make the dialog's `onOpenChange(false)` on the DisplayBackupCodes step run the same handler as Close, which resets state and clears `backupCodes`.

issues.descricao: The default export in BackupCode.tsx is named TwoFactor, a copy-paste leftover from the TOTP component.
issues.textoGolden: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.

comentarios.texto: The default export is named `TwoFactor` but this file (BackupCode.tsx) renders the backup-code field and is imported as `BackupCode` by callers. The copied identifier misstates what the component is; rename the function to `BackupCode` so the name matches the file, the imports and the rendered content.

The default export in BackupCode.tsx is named `TwoFactor`, which is the name of the separate TOTP component. It is a copy-paste leftover and misleads readers and stack traces. Rename it to `BackupCode`.

Component in BackupCode.tsx is named `TwoFactor` (`export default function TwoFactor`) while the file is BackupCode.tsx and it is imported as `BackupCode`. The name disagrees with the code's contract and duplicates the real TwoFactor component, misleading callers/readers. Rename to `BackupCode`.

issues.descricao: The backup-code copy e2e test only waits for the success toast, which is shown unconditionally, so it never verifies the clipboard content.

comentarios.texto: This 'copy' test does not verify the copy behaviour it names: it clicks backup-codes-copy and then only waits for the toast-success element. The handler (EnableTwoFactorModal) runs navigator.clipboard.writeText(...) without awaiting it and then calls showToast(...) unconditionally, so the toast appears even when the clipboard write is removed or fails. The assertion therefore passes with the backup-code copy feature broken; assert the actual effect (clipboard content, or that the formatted codes reached writeText) instead of the toast.

The copy test only waits for a success toast, but the implementation emits that toast unconditionally without awaiting navigator.clipboard.writeText. Removing the clipboard write entirely, copying an empty string, or rejecting the write would still pass this test. Read the clipboard after the click and compare its contents with the displayed backup codes so the test verifies the actual copy effect.
Copy test only waits for toast-success, explicitly TODOing clipboard check. Broken writeText (wrong format/empty) still passes; assert clipboard content equals formatted backup codes.

issues.descricao: Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write, so concurrent logins can accept the same backup code more than once or overwrite each other's removal.
issues.textoGolden: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

comentarios.texto: Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write: the code is validated with indexOf (line 144) and only then persisted via prisma.user.update (line 149), with no unique constraint or lock. Two concurrent login requests sending the same valid backup code both read the unchanged row, both pass the indexOf check, and both obtain a session, violating the 'each backup code can be used exactly once' invariant. Consume the code atomically (e.g. a conditional update on the raw encrypted value / a dedicated used-backup-codes table with a unique index) so only one request can succeed.

Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write, breaking the stated invariant that each backup code is single-use. Two concurrent login requests with the same backup code both read the same user.backupCodes array and both pass `index !== -1` before either `prisma.user.update` commits; both then persist a stale array (each nulling only its own index), so the code authenticates twice. Make consumption atomic (e.g. compare-and-swap on the encrypted value/updatedAt, a transaction with a conditional update, or an optimistic-locking retry) so exactly one request can claim a given code.

Backup-code consumption overwrites the encrypted list by user ID without checking that the stored list still matches the value read before verification. Concurrent requests can both authenticate with the same single-use code, and requests using different codes can overwrite each other's removals and restore a consumed code. Use a conditional atomic update matching the original backupCodes ciphertext and reject or retry authentication if no row was updated.

issues.descricao: The copy button shows a success toast without awaiting clipboard.writeText, so a failed copy still tells the user their backup codes were saved.

comentarios.texto: The handler shows “Backup codes copied!” immediately after calling `navigator.clipboard.writeText`, without awaiting its promise. If clipboard access is denied or the write otherwise rejects, the user still receives a success message and may close the dialog believing their recovery codes were saved. Await the clipboard write and show the success toast only after it resolves; handle rejection with an appropriate translated failure message.

issues.descricao: The download e2e test checks only the filename, not that the file contains the displayed backup codes.

comentarios.texto: The download assertion checks only the static filename from the anchor's download attribute. It still passes if the blob contains empty or incorrect backup codes, leaving the essential recovery-code export behavior unverified. Read the downloaded file and compare its contents to the displayed codes, including their formatting.

Download test only asserts suggestedFilename, explicitly TODOing file-content check. Empty/wrong backupCodes blob with correct filename still passes; assert downloaded file lines equal displayed/formatted backup codes.

issues.descricao: The disable endpoint's error log says 'backup code login' although it is disabling 2FA.

issues.descricao: resetState does not clear backup codes/secret or revoke the backup-codes object URL, leaving a small blob URL leaked per setup cycle.
issues.textoGolden: Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: resetState() clears only password/error/step and never clears backupCodes, secret, dataUri, nor revokes backupCodesUrl. WHY: Closing the modal after setup leaves TOTP secret and backup codes in memory and leaks the Blob object URL on every setup/close cycle. HOW: Clear those states and call URL.revokeObjectURL in resetState and on unmount.

issues.descricao: The disable endpoint calls replaceAll on req.body.backupCode without checking it is a string, so non-string input throws a 500.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: req.body.backupCode.replaceAll assumes a string with no type guard. WHY: A non-string JSON value (number/array) throws TypeError and returns 500 instead of the 400 IncorrectBackupCode contract, breaking error handling and enabling error-probing. HOW: Validate typeof backupCode === 'string' (or String(...)) before replaceAll.

issues.descricao: Backup codes are matched case-sensitively against lowercase hex, so a user typing the code in uppercase is rejected.
issues.textoGolden: Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

issues.descricao: The backup code is compared with the stored codes through Array.indexOf, which is not constant-time and leaks timing information about the secret backup codes.

sugestoes.texto: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases only the column, not the bound `host` value, so a row stored with uppercase characters (e.g. `EvilTrout.com` entered via the admin form, which validates with `/i` and does not downcase) will never match a lowercase referer host and the embed is rejected even though the host is configured. The old `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` compared values verbatim, so this normalization regression is introduced here and silently breaks the `ensure_embeddable` authorization gate in `EmbedController` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`. Bind the downcased value instead: `where("lower(host) = ?", host.downcase)`, or normalize in a `before_validation`/`before_save` callback.

`EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns `nil` for a stale or foreign id, and the following `host.destroy` raises `NoMethodError`, turning a missing record into a 500 instead of a 404. Guard the lookup (e.g. `raise Discourse::NotFound unless host`) before destroying; the same unguarded lookup in `#update` (line 10) feeds `nil` into `save_host` and crashes on `host.host = ...` for the same reason.

issues.descricao: EmbeddableHost's before_validation calls self.host.sub! unconditionally, so saving a record with a nil host raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error.
issues.textoGolden: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

comentarios.texto: The before_validation callback calls `sub!` on host without guarding nil. Creating a host with a missing or null host field reaches this callback from save_host and raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error. Guard nil during normalization and let presence/format validation reject it.

WHAT: `before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally, so a record with a nil host raises NoMethodError (`nil.sub!`) instead of producing a normal format-invalid result. WHY: `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` directly; any request that omits the host value makes the save raise a 500 instead of returning the `render_json_error(host)` validation response. HOW: guard the mutation, e.g. `return if host.blank?` at the top of the before_validation block (or use `self.host = self.host.to_s` before stripping).

before_validation calls self.host.sub!(...) on a possibly-nil host before validates_format_of runs. The controller assigns host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host], so a request without a host key leaves it nil and nil.sub! raises NoMethodError at save time instead of the format validation producing a normal error response. Add a presence guard so validation reports the failure.

issues.descricao: update and destroy in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController fetch the host with where(id:).first and never check for nil, so an unknown id raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of not-found.
issues.textoGolden: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.

comentarios.texto: In the destroy action, the nil-host case (line 15-16) would raise NoMethodError. Consider adding a nil check to handle the case where the host is not found.

update and destroy fetch the record with EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first but never check for nil, then immediately use it (save_host(host) does host.host = ... / host.save; destroy does host.destroy). A stale or already-deleted id, or an interleaving where a concurrent delete removes the row first, makes host nil and the first call on it raises NoMethodError -> unhandled 500. Guard with a nil/404 check before use.

Update passes the nullable result of where(...).first directly to save_host, which immediately assigns host.host. Updating a nonexistent or concurrently deleted record returns an internal error instead of a not-found response; destroy has the same lookup failure. Use find or explicitly raise a not-found error before dereferencing the lookup result.

issues.descricao: record_for_host compares lower(host) against the un-lowercased URI host, so mixed-case referer hosts fail to match allowed hosts and embedding is rejected.
issues.textoGolden: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

comentarios.texto: Normalize the parsed hostname before comparing it with lower(host). URI parsing preserves hostname case, so an allowed entry such as example.com does not match https://EXAMPLE.com/page even though DNS hostnames are case-insensitive. This makes valid embedding requests fail the host authorization check and makes category lookup inconsistent for equivalent domain identities. Compare against host.downcase (or normalize both operands equivalently), and add a mixed-case URL test.

The query compares lower(host) to the un-downcased uri.host. A referer such as http://EvilTrout.com never matches the stored lowercase host, so embedding is wrongly denied. Fix: use where("lower(host) = ?", host.downcase).

The query compares lower(host) in the database with uri.host, which is not lowercased, so the comparison normalizes only one side. A referer or URL with uppercase letters (e.g. http://EvilTrout.com) will not match the stored host. Compare against host.downcase, i.e. where('lower(host) = ?', host.downcase).

issues.descricao: The migration copies the legacy embeddable_hosts values into the new table without stripping scheme and path, so hosts stored as http://example.com no longer match the bare-host lookup and previously allowed embeds are rejected after upgrade.
issues.textoGolden: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: migration inserts raw embeddable_hosts lines (e.g. http://example.com/123) without stripping scheme/path like the model does. WHY: migrated rows never match EmbeddableHost.record_for_host which compares bare uri.host, silently breaking previously allowed embeds.

Migration INSERTs raw embeddable_hosts lines with scheme/path intact, but EmbeddableHost normalizes to bare domain (before_validation strips protocol/path, record_for_host looks up by URI.host). Strip protocol and path before INSERT or migrated hosts will never satisfy host_allowed?.

Legacy hosts are inserted verbatim instead of applying the new model's scheme/path normalization. Existing values such as http://discourse.org or https://example.com/1234 remain in the table, while record_for_host compares only URI.host, so previously configured embedding hosts stop working after upgrade. Normalize migrated entries to the same representation used by the model before inserting them.

issues.textoGolden: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.
